session.question: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
session.answer:
Elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and chromosomal anomalies was associated with a Klinefelter syndrome (KS) phenotype characterized by lower average testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, and higher luteinizing hormone (LH) and FSH levels. Gynecomastia was common in KS and absent in the undefined-cause group. KS patients also had greater height and arm span than men with undefined NOA causes. (riccetto2022clinicalandlaboratory chunk 1)

In testicular XX disorder of sex development (XX DSD), LH and FSH levels and penile length were intermediate between KS and the undefined-cause group. Testicular volume in XX DSD was similar to KS, whereas the remaining clinical findings were closer to those seen in the undefined-cause group. Overall, elevated FSH appears to be a distinguishing laboratory feature of chromosomal-anomaly NOA, especially KS. (riccetto2022clinicalandlaboratory chunk 1)

pqac-a2fad02b: This retrospective study compared men with non-obstructive azoospermia due to chromosomal anomalies versus undefined causes. Among 107 cases, 22 had chromosomal anomalies and 79 had undefined causes. The Klinefelter syndrome (KS) group showed lower average testicular volume, shorter penile length, and lower total testosterone, but higher height, arm span, serum LH and FSH levels, and more frequent gynecomastia than the undefined group. In testicular XX DSD, LH, FSH, and penile length were intermediate between KS and undefined causes; testicular volume was similar to KS, while other findings were more like the undefined group. The study indicates elevated FSH is a distinguishing laboratory feature in chromosomal anomaly cases, especially KS.
From Luísa Riccetto, Tarsis Paiva Vieira, Nilma Lucia Viguetti-Campos, Tais Nitsch Mazzola, Mara Sanches Guaragna, Helena Fabbri-Scallet, Maricilda Palandi de Mello, Antonia Paula Marques-de-Faria, Andrea Trevas Maciel-Guerra, and Gil Guerra. Clinical and laboratory differences between chromosomal and undefined causes of non-obstructive azoospermia: a retrospective study. São Paulo Medical Journal, 2022. pqac-6dc07d2c: The excerpt describes a study of 111 men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) undergoing microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (mTESE). Clinical and endocrine variables assessed included age, BMI, testicular volume, testosterone, FSH, LH, prolactin, SHBG, FSH/LH ratio, and testosterone/LH ratio. Successful sperm retrieval was associated with larger testicular volume and higher testosterone/LH ratio, while failed retrieval was associated with elevated FSH and LH. Multivariate analysis found T/LH ratio, serum FSH, and bilateral testicular volume to be significant predictors of successful retrieval. The excerpt does not discuss chromosomal anomalies, Klinefelter syndrome, or testicular XX DSD comparisons.
From Tae Jin Kim and Kyo Chul Koo. Testosterone to luteinizing hormone ratio as a potential predictor of sperm retrieval in non-obstructive azoospermia patients. Yonsei Medical Journal, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3349/ymj.2023.0054, doi:10.3349/ymj.2023.0054.

pqac-0541368b: The excerpt is about indications for AZF microdeletion screening and karyotyping in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and severe oligozoospermia. It reports that certain chromosomal abnormalities, including inv(Y), idic(Y), 46,XY,r(Y), idic(Y)(p11.2), and der(Y;autosome), should be referred for AZF deletion screening. It also notes a correlation between sperm count and AZF deletions, with only 1% of men with >1×10^6 sperm/mL having Y chromosome microdeletions. However, it does not provide specific evidence about elevated FSH in NOA with chromosomal anomalies, nor does it compare Klinefelter syndrome (KS) and testicular XX DSD versus an undefined-cause group in clinical/laboratory findings.
From Hamid Kalantari, Marjan Sabbaghian, Paraskevi Vogiatzi, Amarnath Rambhatla, Ashok Agarwal, Giovanni M. Colpi, and Mohammad Ali Sadighi Gilani. Bridging the gap between azf microdeletions and karyotype: twelve years’ experience of an infertility center. The World Journal of Men's Health, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.5534/wjmh.220089, doi:10.5534/wjmh.220089.
